newsitem.title: USA: Former U.S. Rep. Cooley lied to Oregon voters.
newsitem.headline: Former U.S. Rep. Cooley lied to Oregon voters.

text.p: Former U.S. Representative Wes Cooley was found guilty Tuesday of lying about his Korean War record in a state voters' pamphlet, the Oregonian newspaper reported.

Cooley was ordered to pay a $5,000 fine and $2,110 in prosecution expenses, complete 100 hours of community service and remain on probation for two years. He escaped a prison sentence under an agreement with prosecutors, the Oregonian reported.

Assistant State Attorney General Byron Chatfield said Cooley agreed to a set of facts that would have proved he never served in Korea, as he had claimed. In a 1994 voters' pamphlet, Cooley claimed he had served in "Army Special Forces, Korea."
Cooley was found guilty by Circuit Judge Al Norblad at a hearing in the state capital of Salem.
"There is no question at all that the defendant never went to Korea," the paper quoted Chatfield as saying. "What he is is a convicted felon."
The maximum penalty for lying in an official document is five years in prison and a $100,000 fine. A second charge of lying in the voters' pamphlet was dropped.
Cooley, a Republican, withdrew from seeking a second term last year under pressure from party leaders over the allegations. Republican Bob Smith, Cooley's predecessor, easily recaptured the seat.
